target.title: fix(active-memory): keep recall circuit breaker tripped across cooldown
target.body:
Closes #100167

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where agents with the `active-memory` plugin enabled pay a fixed recall-timeout stall (~15s by default) on **every** turn once recall starts failing, instead of the plugin backing off. The reporter saw `status=timeout summaryChars=0` on every `main`-agent turn for 24+ hours, making latency-sensitive flows (Talk / live voice, direct chat) feel unresponsive.

The plugin already has a circuit breaker (#74054) that is supposed to skip recall after `circuitBreakerMaxTimeouts` consecutive timeouts. But on cooldown expiry it **deleted the failure record entirely**. At normal turn cadence — turns spaced further apart than `circuitBreakerCooldownMs` (default 60s, max 10m) — the consecutive-timeout count reset to zero before it could ever reach the threshold, so the breaker never re-engaged and every turn ran the sub-agent into the watchdog again.

## Why This Change Was Made

Make the breaker **half-open** across the cooldown instead of resetting ([`extensions/active-memory/index.ts`](extensions/active-memory/index.ts)):

- After the cooldown, allow a single **probe** recall through but keep the tripped record. A probe timeout re-opens the breaker immediately (one recorded timeout, not `maxTimeouts` fresh ones); a successful recall clears it via the existing `resetCircuitBreaker` path.
- Track the in-flight probe so only one runs at a time, and **self-heal**: if a probe is lost (aborted without recording a timeout or success), another is allowed once a full cooldown has elapsed — the breaker can never stick permanently open and silently disable recall.

## User Impact

A persistently failing agent/model now pays the recall timeout **at most once per cooldown window** instead of on every turn. Recovery is unchanged — the next successful recall clears the breaker. Existing config (`circuitBreakerMaxTimeouts`, `circuitBreakerCooldownMs`) is unchanged; docs updated to describe the half-open behavior.

## Scope / Honest Limitations

This is deliberately scoped to the **recurring per-turn timeout tax**, which is the measurable user impact. It does **not** change *why* the embedded recall run produces zero model output (`payloads=0`, `stopReason=missing`) on the reporter's specific stack (openai `gpt-5.5` + codex app-server + `lossless-claw` per-turn projection).

Notably, the issue's suggested root cause (empty prompt from `assembledMessages: 0`) does not hold up in code: [`context-engine-projection.ts`](extensions/codex/src/app-server/context-engine-projection.ts) falls back to the raw recall prompt as `promptText` when there is no assembled context, and that text is sent to Codex — so the prompt is not empty. Pinning down the real zero-output cause needs a live repro on that provider stack, which is why triage labeled the issue `needs-live-repro`. That part is left for a follow-up with live evidence.

One known limitation of this fix: turns spaced further apart than the maximum cooldown (10m) still probe on each turn by design; operators on very low-cadence chats can raise `circuitBreakerCooldownMs` to widen protection.

## Evidence

Focused unit tests added in [`extensions/active-memory/index.test.ts`](extensions/active-memory/index.test.ts):

- After the cooldown, one probe is allowed through, the tripped record is retained (not deleted), and a **single** probe timeout re-opens the breaker immediately — the exact regression behind #100167.
- A lost half-open probe lets another probe through after a further cooldown (no permanent stick), and a successful recall clears the breaker.

Existing breaker tests (skip-within-cooldown, `circuit breaker open` log, reset-on-success) remain valid under the new behavior.

> Note: I could not run the suite locally — this monorepo requires `pnpm@11` and Node `>=22.19` (not available in my environment), so CI runs the tests.
